The behavior tree facilitates a robot's navigation by implementing a fallback mechanism to achieve its tasks. 
It first attempts to compute and follow a path using the A* algorithm to reach a designated goal (goal1). 
If this sequence is unsuccessful, it tries to compute a path to a second goal (goal2) using the Dijkstra algorithm before following it. 
If both attempts to reach the goals fail, the robot will move to a predefined location called "Base." 
This structure ensures that the robot has multiple options to achieve successful navigation, providing robustness and flexibility in its operational environment.

Actions: [ComputePathToPose (parameters: goal, path, planner_id), FollowPath (parameters: path, controller_id), MoveTo (parameters: name, location)]
output:
<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
        <Fallback>
            <Sequence>
                <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal1}" path="{path1}" planner_id="AStar"/>
                <FollowPath path="{path1}" controller_id="FollowPath1"/>
            </Sequence>
            <Sequence>
                <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal2}" path="{path2}" planner_id="Dijkstra"/>
                <FollowPath path="{path2}" controller_id="FollowPath2"/>
            </Sequence>
            <MoveTo name="return_to_base" location="Base"/>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Next, the behavior tree checks whether the robot is stuck. If it is, the robot will stop and execute recovery maneuvers to regain mobility. Lastly, the robot computes a path to the desired endpoints and follows that path while continuously updating it as necessary. This ensures that the robot can adapt to its environment dynamically while navigating.

            <UpdatePath/>

        </ParallelNode>
      </Sequence>

The behavior tree implements a robotic patrolling system in which the robot continuously monitors its environment for specific objects, specifically tomato cans. The robot operates in a "PatrollingMode," wherein it repeatedly moves to a predefined position to prepare its arm and then scans both a table and shelves. During the scanning of the table, it adjusts its torso height and head orientation, pauses for scanning operations, clears any stored octomaps, gathers results of detected items, and updates its planning scene. It also adjusts its height and angle to scan the shelves similarly. This patrol enhances the robot's ability to locate and identify items in its surroundings continuously.

Actions: [GetArmJointsForPose (parameters: pose, joints_pose), SetArmJointsLeft (parameters: joints_pose), SetArmJointsRight (parameters: joints_pose), TorsoControl (parameters: relative_height), HeadControl (parameters: pitch, yaw), Pause (parameters: time_limit_sec), ScanTableStartScanning, ScanTableGetResults (parameters: detected_tomato_cans), TraySetLoci (parameters: tray_name, locus_poses, occupied), TrayUpdatePlanningScene, ScanShelves (parameters: tomato_can_stocking_target_poses), MoveBase (parameters: goal), TrayPickOccupiedLocus (parameters: tray_name, side, locus_id), TrayPickEmptyLocus (parameters: tray_name, side, locus_id, locus_pose), PickAndPlaceRight (parameters: object_id, target_pose, flat_hand_mode), TraySetLocusState (parameters: tray_name, locus_id, occupied).]

    <BehaviorTree ID="root">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTree ID="PatrollingMode" />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="PatrollingMode">
        <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
            <Sequence>
                <SubTree ID="GetInUpTrayPose" />
                <SubTree ID="ScanTable" />
                <SubTree ID="ScanShelves" />
            </Sequence>
        </Repeat>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="GetInUpTrayPose">
        <Sequence>
            <GetArmJointsForPose pose="UPTRAY" joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
            <Parallel success_threshold="2" failure_threshold="2">
                <SetArmJointsLeft joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
                <SetArmJointsRight joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
            </Parallel>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="ClearAllOctomaps">
        <ForceSuccess>
            <Sequence>
                <ClearOctomap side="left" />
                <ClearOctomap side="right" />
            </Sequence>
        </ForceSuccess>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="ScanTable">
        <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
            <Sequence>
                <TorsoControl relative_height="0.95" />
                <HeadControl pitch="0.0" yaw="140.0" />
                <Pause time_limit_sec="3" />
                <ScanTableStartScanning />
                <Pause time_limit_sec="3" />
                <SubTree ID="ClearAllOctomaps" />
                <ScanTableGetResults detected_tomato_cans="{detected_tomato_cans}" />
                <TraySetLoci tray_name="table" locus_poses="{detected_tomato_cans}" occupied="true" />
                <TrayUpdatePlanningScene />
            </Sequence>
        </Repeat>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="ScanShelves">
        <Sequence>
            <TorsoControl relative_height="0.1" />
            <HeadControl pitch="90.0" yaw="90.0" />
            <Pause time_limit_sec="1" />
            <ScanShelves tomato_can_stocking_target_poses="{tomato_can_stocking_target_poses}" />
            <TraySetLoci tray_name="shelf" locus_poses="{tomato_can_stocking_target_poses}" occupied="false" />
            <TrayUpdatePlanningScene />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="FillYourTray">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTree ID="GoToTable" />
            <SubTree ID="ScanTable" />
            <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
                <Sequence>
                    <SubTree ID="TrayIsEmpty" tray="table" side="RIGHT" />
                    <ForceSuccess>
                        <SetBlackboard output_key="src_tray" value="table" />
                        <SetBlackboard output_key="dst_tray" value="backtray" />
                        <SubTree ID="RightArmFillYourTray" src_tray="src_tray" dst_tray="dst_tray" />
                    </ForceSuccess>
                </Sequence>
            </Repeat>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="GoToTable">
        <Sequence>
            <MoveBase goal="1.5;-0.1;0.0" />
            <MoveBase goal="2.2;-0.1;0.0" />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="RightArmFillYourTray">
        <Sequence>
            <TrayPickOccupiedLocus tray_name="{src_tray}" side="RIGHT" locus_id="{src_locus_id}" />
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <TrayPickEmptyLocus tray_name="{dst_tray}" side="RIGHT" locus_id="{dst_locus_id}" locus_pose="{dst_locus_pose}" />
                    <PickAndPlaceRight object_id="{src_locus_id}" target_pose="{dst_locus_pose}" flat_hand_mode="false" />
                    <TraySetLocusState tray_name="{src_tray}" locus_id="{src_locus_id}" occupied="false" />
                    <TraySetLocusState tray_name="{dst_tray}" locus_id="{dst_locus_id}" occupied="true" />
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

This process is repeated up to two times at a rate of 2 Hz. Following path computation, the robot attempts to follow the newly generated path and clears the local costmap. If challenges arise during this process, the system enters a recovery phase, where it clears the local costmap, spins in place to reassess the surroundings, and waits for one second to allow for any changes in the environment. The overall design enhances the robot's ability to navigate complex environments by continually updating its course and managing obstacles effectively.

In combat situations, if the entity is under attack or has a hunt target, it will abort the current job. It then determines the enemy's position, moves towards it, and engages in combat if within range. 

For jobs like harvesting an animal, it prepares to harvest by moving to the location, selecting the animal, and finally packaging it before finishing the job. If the job type isn’t as expected, it aborts.

This structured hierarchy enables the entity to manage tasks efficiently while adapting to dynamic scenarios.

Once the path is computed, the robot attempts to follow it, continuing until a failure occurs. 
If the robot fails to navigate successfully, it activates a recovery process, which may involve clearing both local and global costmaps to reset the environment perception and recalculating a new path using Dijkstra's algorithm. 
This behavior allows the robot to adapt to dynamic or unforeseen challenges during its navigation task.

The behavior tree describes a monitoring system for a robotic entity, overseeing its operational status and managing potential errors. The process begins with configuring the monitoring parameters based on the entity's current state—either "CHARGING" or "OPERATING"—and responding with appropriate actions, such as speaking a greeting or changing facial expressions. It then enters the main monitoring phase, where it continuously checks conditions and responds to different statuses, like info, warnings, and errors, and updates a blackboard accordingly. If specific conditions are met, it may restart nodes or handle errors related to the RTABMap system, ensuring the robot adapts its operations or resolves issues effectively.

Actions: [Monitoring (parameters: blocked_groups, description, error_level, key), ReconfigureMonitoring (parameters: parameter_set, parameter_set_out), Speak (parameters: text), FacialExpression (parameters: duration, expression), SetKillGroups (parameters: curr_kill_group, parameter_set), KillNodeFromGroup (parameters: group, kill_node), KillROSNode (parameters: node), StatusToParamServer (parameters: description, key, rewrite_stamp), RotateToRelocalize (parameters: none), SaveTimestamp (parameters: timestamp), ROSOut (parameters: level, msg), GroupFromKey (parameters: group, key), LaunchFileFromGroup (parameters: group, launch_file, pkg), StartLaunchFile (parameters: blocked_groups, group_block, launch_file, pkg)]
output:
<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="Monitoring">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTree ID="ConfigureMonitoring" __shared_blackboard="false" rtabmap_strike="rtabmap_strike"/>
            <Action ID="Monitoring" blocked_groups="{blocked_groups}" description="{desc}" error_level="{err}" key="{key}"/>
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <Condition ID="NodeMonitor" description="{desc}"/>
                    <SubTree ID="RestartNode" __shared_blackboard="false" blocked_groups="blocked_groups" desc="desc" key="key" status="status"/>
                </Sequence>
                <Sequence>
                    <Condition ID="RTABMapMonitor" description="{desc}"/>
                    <SubTree ID="RTABMapHandling" __shared_blackboard="false" key="key" rtabmap_strike="rtabmap_strike" status="status"/>
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="ConfigureMonitoring">
        <Sequence>
            <IfThenElse>
                <Condition ID="Charging"/>
                <Fallback>
                    <BlackboardCheckString return_on_mismatch="FAILURE" value_A="{parameter_set}" value_B="CHARGING">
                        <AlwaysSuccess/>
                    </BlackboardCheckString>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="ReconfigureMonitoring" parameter_set="CHARGING" parameter_set_out="{parameter_set}"/>
                        <Action ID="Speak" text="Gute Nacht!"/>
                        <Action ID="FacialExpression" duration="10000" expression="SLEEP"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
                <Fallback>
                    <BlackboardCheckString return_on_mismatch="FAILURE" value_A="{parameter_set}" value_B="OPERATING">
                        <AlwaysSuccess/>
                    </BlackboardCheckString>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="ReconfigureMonitoring" parameter_set="OPERATING" parameter_set_out="{parameter_set}"/>
                        <Action ID="Speak" text="Guten Morgen!"/>
                        <Action ID="FacialExpression" duration="5.0" expression="NEUTRAL"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
            </IfThenElse>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="KillRemainingNodes">
        <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
            <Sequence>
                <Action ID="SetKillGroups" curr_kill_group="{curr_group}" parameter_set="{parameter_set}"/>
                <ForceSuccess>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="KillNodeFromGroup" group="{curr_group}" kill_node="{curr_node}"/>
                        <Action ID="KillROSNode" node="{curr_node}"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </ForceSuccess>
            </Sequence>
        </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="ProcessStatus">
        <Fallback>
            <Sequence>
                <Condition ID="StatusInfo" description="{desc}" error_level="{err}" key="{key}"/>
                <Action ID="StatusToParamServer" description="{desc}" key="{key}" rewrite_stamp="true"/>
                <SetBlackboard output_key="status" value="INFO"/>
                <Action ID="ROSOut" level="INFO" msg="Everything ok!" throttle_period="120"/>
            </Sequence>
            <Sequence>
                <Condition ID="StatusWarn" description="{desc}" error_level="{err}" key="{key}"/>
                <Action ID="StatusToParamServer" description="{desc}" key="{key}" rewrite_stamp="true"/>
                <SetBlackboard output_key="status" value="WARN"/>
            </Sequence>
            <Sequence>
                <Condition ID="StatusError" description="{desc}" error_level="{err}" key="{key}"/>
                <Action ID="StatusToParamServer" description="{desc}" key="{key}" rewrite_stamp="false"/>
                <SetBlackboard output_key="status" value="ERROR"/>
            </Sequence>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="RTABMapHandling">
        <Fallback>
            <BlackboardCheckString return_on_mismatch="FAILURE" value_A="INFO" value_B="{status}">
                <SetBlackboard name="ResetStrike" output_key="rtabmap_strike" value="0"/>
            </BlackboardCheckString>
            <BlackboardCheckString return_on_mismatch="FAILURE" value_A="ERROR" value_B="{status}">
                <Switch4 case_1="0" case_2="1" case_3="2" case_4="3" name="SwitchStrikeCase" variable="{rtabmap_strike}">
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="RotateToRelocalize"/>
                        <Action ID="SaveTimestamp" timestamp="{timestamp}"/>
                        <SetBlackboard name="SetFirstStrike" output_key="rtabmap_strike" value="1"/>
                    </Sequence>
                    <ForceSuccess>
                        <Sequence>
                            <Action ID="SaveTimestamp" timestamp="{timestamp}"/>
                            <SetBlackboard output_key="key" value="/rtabmap/rtabmap"/>
                            <Action ID="ROSOut" level="INFO" msg="Killing RTABMap nodes" throttle_period="0"/>
                            <Sequence>
                                <Action ID="GroupFromKey" group="{group}" key="{key}"/>
                                <Action ID="KillNodeFromGroup" group="{group}" kill_node="{kill_node}"/>
                                <Action ID="KillROSNode" node="{kill_node}"/>
                            </Sequence>
                        </Sequence>
                    </ForceSuccess>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="RotateToRelocalize"/>
                        <Action ID="SaveTimestamp" timestamp="{timestamp}"/>
                        <SetBlackboard name="SetSecondStrike" output_key="rtabmap_strike" value="2"/>
                    </Sequence>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="RotateToRelocalize"/>
                        <Action ID="SaveTimestamp" timestamp="{timestamp}"/>
                        <SetBlackboard name="SetThirdStrike" output_key="rtabmap_strike" value="3"/>
                    </Sequence>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Fallback>
                            <Condition ID="TimePassed" duration="60" timestamp="{timestamp}"/>
                            <ForceFailure>
                                <Action ID="RotateToRelocalize"/>
                            </ForceFailure>
                        </Fallback>
                        <IfThenElse name="IfSuccesfulReset">
                            <Action ID="CallSupervisor" message="{localization_msg}"/>
                            <SetBlackboard name="ResetStrike" output_key="rtabmap_strike" value="0"/>
                        </IfThenElse>
                    </Sequence>
                    <AlwaysSuccess/>
                </Switch4>
            </BlackboardCheckString>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="RestartNode">
        <BlackboardCheckString name="CheckIfError" return_on_mismatch="FAILURE" value_A="{status}" value_B="ERROR">
            <Sequence>
                <Action ID="GroupFromKey" group="{group}" key="{key}"/>
                <Fallback>
                    <Condition ID="GroupNotBlocked" blocked_groups="{blocked_groups}" group="{group}"/>
                    <ForceFailure>
                        <Action ID="ROSOut" level="INFO" msg="Group still blocked. Restart process skipped." throttle_period="0"/>
                    </ForceFailure>
                </Fallback>
                <Fallback>
                    <Sequence name="KillSequence">
                        <Action ID="KillNodeFromGroup" group="{group}" kill_node="{kill_node}"/>
                        <Action ID="KillROSNode" node="{kill_node}"/>
                    </Sequence>
                    <Sequence name="LaunchSequence">
                        <Action ID="LaunchFileFromGroup" group="{group}" launch_file="{launch_file}" pkg="{pkg}"/>
                        <Action ID="StartLaunchFile" blocked_groups="{blocked_groups}" group_block="{group}" launch_file="{launch_file}" pkg="{pkg}"/>
                        <Action ID="ROSOut" level="INFO" msg="Launch file started" throttle_period="0"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
            </Sequence>
        </BlackboardCheckString>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Once the path is established, it follows the route and cleans the local cost map for real-time updates.

In "JobStandardPatrol," the agent initializes a job, claims items, and concurrently moves while finding a tool. The agent then equips the tool and attempts to pick up items until all necessary items are in place, followed by moving, working, and finishing the job.

This structure ensures that the agent can effectively manage its needs while also fulfilling job responsibilities.

If not, it proceeds to retrieve the next goal from a predefined list. Upon receiving a goal, the system attempts to navigate to the specified pose. If navigation fails, a recovery mechanism is triggered that allows for one retry and includes a wait period of 7 seconds before trying again. The process continues to loop until the goal is achieved, at which point it updates the status indicating that the current goal has been accomplished. This design is effective for robots or agents that need to adaptively follow a series of waypoints while handling possible failures in navigation.

Actions: [GetNextGoal (parameters: goals, goal, goal_achieved), NavigateToPose (parameters: goal), Wait (parameters: wait_duration), SetBlackboard (parameters: output_key, value)]
output:
<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="DynamicWaypointFollow">
        <ReactiveFallback>
            <AllGoalsAchieved goal_achieved="{goal_achieved}"/>
            <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
                <Parallel success_count="1" failure_count="1">
                    <GetNextGoal goals="{goals}" goal="{goal}" goal_achieved="{goal_achieved}"/>
                    <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1">
                        <NavigateToPose goal="{goal}"/>
                        <Wait wait_duration="7"/>
                    </RecoveryNode>
                </Parallel>
                <SetBlackboard output_key="goal_achieved" value="true"/>
            </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
        </ReactiveFallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

It first attempts to get a float64 number from the specified topic "/numbers." 
If successful, it compares this number to see if it is greater than or equal to 5. 
If the number meets this condition, a debug message indicating that the number is larger or equal to 5 is logged; otherwise, it logs that the number is less than 5. 
If the initial retrieval of the number fails, the robot prompts the user with a message asking for a number. 
Finally, after handling the number comparison, the robot verbally requests a number using a predefined utterance in English.

The robot aims to explore its environment by first calculating a path to a designated exploration goal using the Dijkstra algorithm and following that path with an exploration-specific controller. 
If the exploration sequence fails, the robot attempts a backup navigation strategy: it computes a path to a backup goal via the A* algorithm and uses a recovery path controller to follow this second path. 
This structure ensures the robot can adaptively explore its surroundings while having a contingency plan for navigation if initial attempts do not succeed.

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <Fallback name="ExploreAndNavigate">
      <Sequence>
        <SpeedController min_rate="0.3" max_rate="0.7" min_speed="0.15" max_speed="0.4" filter_duration="0.4">
          <ComputePathToPose goal="{exploration_goal}" path="{exploration_path}" planner_id="Dijkstra"/>
        </SpeedController>
        <FollowPath path="{exploration_path}" controller_id="ExplorePathController"/>
      </Sequence>
      <Sequence>
        <SpeedController min_rate="0.1" max_rate="0.3" min_speed="0.05" max_speed="0.2" filter_duration="0.5">
          <ComputePathToPose goal="{backup_goal}" path="{backup_path}" planner_id="AStar"/>
        </SpeedController>
        <FollowPath path="{backup_path}" controller_id="RecoveryPathFollowing"/>
      </Sequence>
    </Fallback>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Initially, the robot moves to a base position at coordinates (1, 1) and then positions its arm at (150, 150, 0) while setting its gripper to an open state. 
The robot then waits for a user confirmation to start the exploration, accepting a response of either 'y' or 'n'. Upon receiving a 'yes', it proceeds to move to another base position at (4, 4). 
If an obstacle is detected, the robot requests confirmation to continue exploring. It again accepts 'y' or 'n' as input and, following a positive response, it retracts its arm and gripper to a position of (0, 0, 0) and closes the gripper. Finally, it moves to a neutral base position of (0, 0).

Actions: [BaseMovement (parameters: x, y), ArmMovement (parameters: x, y, z, gripper_position), StringParameterRequest (parameters: title, msg, value)]
output:
<root main_tree_to_execute="ExplorationPath" BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="ExplorationPath">
        <Sequence>
            <BaseMovement x="1" y="1"/>
            <ArmMovement x="150" y="150" z="0" gripper_position="1"/>
            <Repeater>
                <StringParameterRequest title="Ready for exploration?" 
                                        msg="type [y] or [n]"
                                        value="{confirm}"/>
                <CheckBlackboard input="{confirm}" compare_to="y" />
            </Repeater>
            <BaseMovement x="4" y="4"/>
            <StringParameterRequest title="Found an obstacle, should I continue?" 
                                    msg="type [y] or [n]"
                                    value="{confirm}"/>
            <CheckBlackboard input="{confirm}" compare_to="y" />
            <ArmMovement x="0" y="0" z="0" gripper_position="0"/>
            <BaseMovement x="0" y="0"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The tree also includes recovery actions if the robot detects that it is stuck, which involves stopping and spinning. 

For navigation, the robot computes a path to a given endpoint and follows this path. It continuously updates the path while following it, ensuring adaptability to dynamic environments.

Within this sequence, a fallback mechanism is implemented to either compute a path to a specified exploration area at a frequency of 1 Hz or check the surroundings for any potential obstacles or important features. Once a viable path is established or the surroundings are analyzed, the robot proceeds to follow the computed exploration path. The sequence concludes when the robot successfully reaches its designated goal, ensuring a thorough exploration of the area. 

Actions: [ComputePathToPose (parameters: goal), CheckSurroundings, FollowPath (parameters: path), GoalReached]
output:
<root main_tree_to_execute="ExplorationTree" BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="ExplorationTree">
        <Sequence name="exploration_sequence">
            <Fallback name="fallback_explore">
                <RateController hz="1.0">
                    <ComputePathToPose goal="${explore_area}"/>
                </RateController>
                <CheckSurroundings/>
            </Fallback>
            <FollowPath path="${exploration_path}"/>
            <GoalReached/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The behavior tree is designed to automate the cleaning process of a coffee machine after brewing. It first checks if the cleaning process is finished. If not, it verifies whether there is enough water available. If the water tank is removed, it waits for it to be placed back in the machine, ensuring it is full before proceeding to fill it up if necessary. Simultaneously, it checks the marro tank's status, ensuring it's either not full or is emptied if removed. 

The cleaning task relies on the successful placement of both tanks back into the coffee machine for proper operation. This structure supports efficient management of resources and conditions to maintain the coffee machine’s cleanliness automatically.

Actions: [FillWaterTank, EmptyMarroTank, PressDesiredCoffe, PlaceCleanCup, SwitchOffCoffeMachine, AddMilktoCoffe, AddSugarToCoffe, SwitchOnCoffeMachine, PlaceCoffeCup]

<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="AutoClean">
        <Fallback>
            <Condition ID="IsCleanProcessFinished"/>
            <Fallback>
                <Condition ID="IsThereEnoughWater"/>
                <Sequence>
                    <Timeout msec="2000">
                        <Condition ID="IsWaterTankRemoved"/>
                    </Timeout>
                    <Fallback>
                        <Timeout msec="1000">
                            <Condition ID="IsWaterTankFull"/>
                        </Timeout>
                        <Action ID="FillWaterTank"/>
                    </Fallback>
                    <RetryUntilSuccesful num_attempts="30">
                        <Condition ID="IsWaterTankPlacedInCoffeMachine"/>
                    </RetryUntilSuccesful>
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
            <Fallback>
                <Inverter>
                    <Condition ID="IsMarroTankFull"/>
                </Inverter>
                <Sequence>
                    <Timeout msec="4000">
                        <Condition ID="IsMarroTankRemoved"/>
                    </Timeout>
                    <Fallback>
                        <Timeout msec="3000">
                            <Condition ID="IsMarroTankEmpty"/>
                        </Timeout>
                        <Action ID="EmptyMarroTank"/>
                    </Fallback>
                    <RetryUntilSuccesful num_attempts="60">
                        <Condition ID="IsMarroTankPlacedInCoffeMachine"/>
                    </RetryUntilSuccesful>
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="MainBehaviorTree">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTree ID="OpenCoffeMachine" __shared_blackboard="false"/>
            <SubTree ID="CoffeType" __shared_blackboard="false"/>
            <SubTree ID="AutoClean" __shared_blackboard="false"/>
            <SubTree ID="PutCoffeCup" __shared_blackboard="false"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="CoffeType">
        <Sequence>
            <Fallback>
                <Timeout msec="2000">
                    <Condition ID="IsDesiredCoffeSelected"/>
                </Timeout>
                <Action ID="PressDesiredCoffe"/>
            </Fallback>
            <Timeout msec="5000">
                <Condition ID="IsCoffeFinished"/>
            </Timeout>
            <Timeout msec="3000">
                <Condition ID="HasCupOffCoffeBeenRemoved"/>
            </Timeout>
            <Timeout msec="3000">
                <Fallback>
                    <Condition ID="HasHumanAddedCleaningCup"/>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="PlaceCleanCup"/>
                        <Action ID="SwitchOffCoffeMachine"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
            </Timeout>
            <Timeout msec="4000">
                <Fallback name="parallel">
                    <Condition ID="HasHumanAddedMilk"/>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Fallback>
                            <Inverter>
                                <Condition ID="IsMilkDesired"/>
                            </Inverter>
                            <Action ID="AddMilktoCoffe"/>
                        </Fallback>
                        <Fallback>
                            <Inverter>
                                <Condition ID="IsSugarDesired"/>
                            </Inverter>
                            <Action ID="AddSugarToCoffe"/>
                        </Fallback>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
            </Timeout>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="OpenCoffeMachine">
        <Fallback>
            <Condition ID="IsMachineOpen"/>
            <Sequence>
                <RetryUntilSuccesful num_attempts="3">
                    <Condition ID="IsCleanCupReady"/>
                </RetryUntilSuccesful>
                <Fallback>
                    <Timeout msec="2000">
                        <Condition ID="IsMachineOpen"/>
                    </Timeout>
                    <Action ID="SwitchOnCoffeMachine"/>
                </Fallback>
            </Sequence>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="PutCoffeCup">
        <Fallback>
            <Timeout msec="3000">
                <Condition ID="IsCoffeCupReady"/>
            </Timeout>
            <Action ID="PlaceCoffeCup"/>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Initially, it checks the status of the door using two conditions: if the door is closed or if it is open, the robot will proceed accordingly. 
If the door is closed, the robot will perform the actions of opening the door followed by passing through it. 
If the door is open, the robot will pass through the door and close it behind itself. 
If the door is not an option (i.e., both conditions fail), the robot can alternatively pass through a window and close the door if it was left open. 
This behavior allows for flexible navigation based on the state of the door.

Actions: [OpenDoor, PassThroughDoor, PassThroughWindow, CloseDoor]

<root BTCPP_format="4" main_tree_to_execute="NavigateTree">
    <BehaviorTree ID="NavigateTree">
        <Sequence>
            <Fallback>
                <Condition ID="IsDoorClosed"/>
                <Inverter>
                    <Condition ID="IsDoorOpen"/>
                </Inverter>
            </Fallback>
            <Sequence>
                <Action ID="OpenDoor"/>
                <Action ID="PassThroughDoor"/>
            </Sequence>
            <Sequence>
                <Action ID="PassThroughWindow"/>
                <Action ID="CloseDoor"/>
            </Sequence>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

After confirming that the battery level is above a threshold (30), it proceeds to truncate the navigational path to ensure it remains manageable, specifically truncating it to a distance of 5.0 units.

                    <Action ID="InquireName"/>

                <Sequence>

It begins by repeatedly attempting to move to two primary goals (1.0, 0.0, 0.0) and (3.0, 0.5, 1.0) until either of them is successfully reached, utilizing a parallel execution structure that requires at least two successes among these movements. Once this task is completed, the robot then enters a fallback mechanism that provides alternative navigation routes if the primary goals are not attainable. It attempts to move to two alternative goals: (2.0, 2.0, 0.0) with a 0.3-meter backtrack, and (0.0, 3.0, 0.0) with a 0.4-meter backtrack. This multi-layered approach ensures the robot can adaptively pursue its objectives while managing its navigation effectively.

    <BehaviorTree ID="goal_priority_tree">
        <Sequence>

                    <MoveBase goal="1.0;0.0;0.0"/>
                    <MoveBase goal="3.0;0.5;1.0"/>
                </Parallel>
            </RepeatUntilSuccess>
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <MoveBase goal="2.0;2.0;0.0"/>
                    <Backtrack target_distance_m="0.3"/>
                </Sequence>
                <Sequence>
                    <MoveBase goal="0.0;3.0;0.0"/>
                    <Backtrack target_distance_m="0.4"/>
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The behavior tree outlines a robotic task focused on patrolling and scanning an area for objects, as well as managing a tray for storage and refilling operations. The robot begins its patrol by transitioning to a low tray pose, followed by scanning the surrounding area for objects and containers. During the scanning process, it retrieves object information and updates its internal representations of the detected objects, which aids in planning for subsequent tasks. Furthermore, the robot is programmed to go to a storage area, scan for containers, and refill its tray from designated sources. The refill process involves picking objects from one tray and placing them into another while updating the status of their occupancy. The patrolling and scanning operations are designed to be repeated indefinitely, ensuring continuous monitoring and management of the environment.

Actions: [GetArmJointsForPose (parameters: pose, joints_pose), SetArmJointsLeft (parameters: joints_pose), SetArmJointsRight (parameters: joints_pose), TorsoControl (parameters: relative_height), HeadControl (parameters: pitch, yaw), Pause (parameters: time_limit_sec), ScanTableStartScanning, ScanTableGetResults (parameters: detected_objects), TraySetLoci (parameters: tray_name, locus_poses, occupied), TrayUpdatePlanningScene, MoveBase (parameters: goal), TrayPickOccupiedLocus (parameters: tray_name, side, locus_id), TrayPickEmptyLocus (parameters: tray_name, side, locus_id, locus_pose), PickAndPlaceLeft (parameters: object_id, target_pose, flat_hand_mode), TraySetLocusState (parameters: tray_name, locus_id, occupied)]

<root main_tree_to_execute="root" BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="root">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTree ID="PatrollingMode" />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="PatrollingMode">
        <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
            <Sequence>
                <SubTree ID="GetInLowTrayPose" />
                <SubTree ID="ScanArea" />
                <SubTree ID="ScanContainers" />
            </Sequence>
        </Repeat>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="GetInLowTrayPose">
        <Sequence>
            <GetArmJointsForPose pose="LOWTRAY" joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
            <Parallel success_threshold="1" failure_threshold="1">
                <SetArmJointsLeft joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
                <SetArmJointsRight joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
            </Parallel>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="ClearSpecificOctomap">
        <ForceSuccess>
            <Sequence>
                <ClearOctomap side="front" />
                <ClearOctomap side="back" />
            </Sequence>
        </ForceSuccess>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="ScanArea">
        <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
            <Sequence>
                <TorsoControl relative_height="0.85" />
                <HeadControl pitch="0.0" yaw="130.0" />
                <Pause time_limit_sec="4" />
                <ScanTableStartScanning />
                <Pause time_limit_sec="4" />
                <SubTree ID="ClearSpecificOctomap" />
                <ScanTableGetResults detected_objects="{detected_objects}" />
                <TraySetLoci tray_name="area" locus_poses="{detected_objects}" occupied="true" />
                <TrayUpdatePlanningScene />
            </Sequence>
        </Repeat>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="ScanContainers">
        <Sequence>
            <TorsoControl relative_height="0.2" />
            <HeadControl pitch="80.0" yaw="80.0" />
            <Pause time_limit_sec="2" />
            <ScanShelves container_target_poses="{container_target_poses}" />
            <TraySetLoci tray_name="containers" locus_poses="{container_target_poses}" occupied="false" />
            <TrayUpdatePlanningScene />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="RefillTray">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTree ID="GoToStorage" />
            <SubTree ID="ScanContainers" />
            <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
                <Sequence>
                    <SubTree ID="TrayIsFull" tray="area" side="LEFT" />
                    <ForceSuccess>
                        <SetBlackboard output_key="source_tray" value="area" />
                        <SetBlackboard output_key="destination_tray" value="fronttray" />
                        <SubTree ID="LeftArmRefillTray" source_tray="source_tray" destination_tray="destination_tray" />
                    </ForceSuccess>
                </Sequence>
            </Repeat>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="GoToStorage">
        <Sequence>
            <MoveBase goal="2.0;0.5;0.0" />
            <MoveBase goal="2.5;0.5;0.0" />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="LeftArmRefillTray">
        <Sequence>
            <TrayPickOccupiedLocus tray_name="{source_tray}" side="LEFT" locus_id="{source_locus_id}" />
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <TrayPickEmptyLocus tray_name="{destination_tray}" side="LEFT" locus_id="{destination_locus_id}" locus_pose="{destination_locus_pose}" />
                    <PickAndPlaceLeft object_id="{source_locus_id}" target_pose="{destination_locus_pose}" flat_hand_mode="false" />
                    <TraySetLocusState tray_name="{source_tray}" locus_id="{source_locus_id}" occupied="false" />
                    <TraySetLocusState tray_name="{destination_tray}" locus_id="{destination_locus_id}" occupied="true" />
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

In detail, the robot first adjusts its arm joints to a "TRAY" pose, then scans tables at a relative height of 0.90 and checks for objects. Detected items are recorded and mapped to the tray as occupied locations. Following table examinations, the robot lowers to a height of 0.15 to scan the shelves, recording any objects found.

The robot continuously prepares its tray pose, inspects tables by scanning, and collects item data in a repeated cycle. 
During the table inspection, it adjusts its torso and head for optimal viewing, pauses for scanning, and updates its information about detected items. 
After inspecting tables, it also inspects shelves, adjusting its position accordingly. 
The robot uses collected data to stock its tray with items from the source tray to the destination tray. 
This process ensures effective item management and spatial awareness within the environment.

    <BehaviorTree ID="root">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTree ID="SurveyMode" />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="SurveyMode">
        <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
            <Sequence>
                <SubTree ID="PrepareTrayPose" />
                <SubTree ID="InspectTables" />
                <SubTree ID="InspectShelves" />
            </Sequence>
        </Repeat>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="PrepareTrayPose">
        <Sequence>
            <GetArmJointsForPose pose="TRAY" joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
            <Parallel success_threshold="3" failure_threshold="1">
                <SetArmJointsLeft joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
                <SetArmJointsRight joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
                <SetArmJointsBoth joints_pose="{joints_pose}" />
            </Parallel>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="PurgeAllOctomaps">
        <ForceSuccess>
            <Sequence>
                <ClearOctomap side="left" />
                <ClearOctomap side="right" />
                <ClearOctomap side="bottom" />
            </Sequence>
        </ForceSuccess>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="InspectTables">
        <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
            <Sequence>
                <TorsoControl relative_height="0.95" />
                <HeadControl pitch="0.0" yaw="120.0" />
                <Pause time_limit_sec="3" />
                <ScanTableStartScanning />
                <Pause time_limit_sec="3" />

                <ScanTableGetResults detected_items="{detected_items}" />
                <TraySetLoci tray_name="table" locus_poses="{detected_items}" occupied="true" />

            <TorsoControl relative_height="0.3" />
            <HeadControl pitch="90.0" yaw="45.0" />
            <Pause time_limit_sec="2" />
            <ScanShelves object_target_poses="{object_target_poses}" />
            <TraySetLoci tray_name="shelf" locus_poses="{object_target_poses}" occupied="false" />
            <TrayUpdatePlanningScene />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

            <SubTree ID="TravelToTable" />
            <SubTree ID="InspectTables" />

                        <SubTree ID="RightHandStockYourTray" source_tray="src_tray" destination_tray="dst_tray" />

            </Repeat>
        </Sequence>

        <Sequence>
            <MoveBase goal="1.5;-0.3;0.0" />
            <MoveBase goal="2.0;-0.3;0.0" />
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

    <BehaviorTree ID="RightHandStockYourTray">
        <Sequence>
            <TrayPickOccupiedLocus tray_name="{src_tray}" side="RIGHT" locus_id="{src_locus_id}" />
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <TrayPickEmptyLocus tray_name="{dst_tray}" side="RIGHT" locus_id="{dst_locus_id}" locus_pose="{dst_locus_pose}" />

                    <TraySetLocusState tray_name="{dst_tray}" locus_id="{dst_locus_id}" occupied="true" />
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

At a frequency of 1 Hz, it computes the path to the target exploration point using the Dijkstra algorithm and prepares to follow that path. Simultaneously, it checks for obstacles with a given probability. The robot is set to follow the exploration path unless it detects an obstacle. If an obstacle is detected or if it cannot proceed, the robot will switch to a fallback behavior where it either moves to a designated safe zone or pauses for a brief waiting period of 3 seconds. This setup enables efficient and safe exploration while dynamically responding to environmental changes.

Actions: [ComputePathToPose (parameters: goal, path, planner_id), FollowPath (parameters: path, controller_id), MoveTo (parameters: location), Wait (parameters: duration)]
output:
<root BTCPP_format="4" main_tree_to_execute="ExplorationTree">
    <BehaviorTree ID="ExplorationTree">
        <Sequence>
            <RateController hz="1.0">
                <ComputePathToPose goal="{exploration_point}" path="{exploration_path}" planner_id="Dijkstra"/>
            </RateController>
            <Parallel success_count="2" failure_count="1">
                <FollowPath path="{exploration_path}" controller_id="ExploreController"/>
                <isObstacleDetected prob="0.2"/>
            </Parallel>
            <Fallback>
                <MoveTo location="SafeZone"/>
                <Wait duration="3"/>
            </Fallback>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Initially, at a frequency of 1 Hz, it updates the goal and computes a path to the updated goal using the A* algorithm. After determining the path, it truncates the path to maintain a manageable distance of 3.0 units. 
The robot then follows this truncated path continuously until a failure occurs, allowing for dynamic adjustments as the environment changes. 
This behavior is essential for safe and efficient navigation in potentially complex surroundings.

    <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
        <PipelineSequence name="PathFinding">
            <RateController hz="1.0">
                <Sequence>
                    <GoalUpdater input_goal="{goal}" output_goal="{updated_goal}">

When a path becomes unfeasible, the system engages a recovery mechanism that involves two main phases: correcting the path and executing the corrected path. 
First, it attempts to update the path using the Dijkstra planner and clears the global costmap to refresh obstacle data. 
Once the path is updated, it executes this path while also clearing the local costmap.

This systematic approach ensures that the robot effectively adapts to changes in the environment while maintaining its trajectory towards the goal.

It utilizes a recovery node with up to five retries to reevaluate the situation. Initially, it computes a new path using the A* algorithm and follows it with a "QuickNavigator," updating the path at a frequency of 2 Hz for timely adjustments. If the goal is updated or additional issues arise, the robot executes a reactive fallback procedure, which includes spinning to potentially reassess its surroundings and waiting for 10 seconds. This hierarchical structure allows the robot to adaptively manage its navigation in changing scenarios.

If that fails, it proceeds with navigation by following the new path while clearing the local costmap. 
Additionally, the behavior tree includes an emergency fallback that triggers if the goal is updated. 
During this fallback, the robot clears the local costmap immediately, waits for 20 seconds, and then performs a spin maneuver.

This sequence attempts to compute a new path towards a specified goal using an RRT planner and clears the global costmap to ensure there are no obstacles detected before planning. If this fails, it retries executing the planned path while also clearing the local costmap. If all recovery attempts fail, the robot engages in a reactive recovery behavior, which includes clearing both local and global maps, spinning to reassess the environment, and waiting to establish a stable state before attempting further navigation. 

This system ensures the robot can adapt and recover effectively when navigating dynamic or uncertain environments.

It begins with a fallback sequence for behavior management, where it first checks for breeding conditions—evaluating if the animal is male and in heat before performing mating. 
If these conditions are not met, it examines feeding conditions to see if the animal is hungry, allowing it to eat if true. 
Additionally, the animal can engage in behaviors from the "ShedTree" sub-tree, which includes actions like surveying the area and feeding during the day, or resting if it is in the shed. 
This design enables the animal to prioritize its behaviors based on its current state and environment.

Actions: [Mate, Eat, SurveyArea, Feed, Rest]

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree" BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
        <FallbackStar name="BehaviorManagement">
            <SequenceStar name="BreedingConditions">
                <Condition ID="IsMale"/>
                <Condition ID="IsInHeat"/>
                <Action ID="Mate"/>
            </SequenceStar>
            <SequenceStar name="FeedingCondition">
                <Condition ID="IsHungry"/>
                <Action ID="Eat"/>
            </SequenceStar>
            <SubTree ID="ShedTree"/>
        </FallbackStar>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="ShedTree">
        <FallbackStar>
            <SequenceStar>
                <Condition ID="IsDay"/>
                <Action ID="SurveyArea"/>
                <Action ID="Feed"/>
            </SequenceStar>
            <SequenceStar>
                <Condition ID="IsInShed"/>
                <Action ID="Rest"/>
            </SequenceStar>
        </FallbackStar>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

At its core, if the character is in combat, it will abort its current job and take actions to get a target, move toward it, and attack if the target is adjacent. Other tasks include checking and equipping a uniform and addressing hunger by finding food, moving if necessary, picking up food items, and eating. Additionally, a job harvesting an animal involves initializing the job, moving to the animal, grabbing it, harvesting, and finally releasing it. The character has various job options, all orchestrated under specific conditions, ensuring effective prioritization between combat readiness, job execution, and personal needs such as hunger and uniform readiness.

    <BehaviorTree ID="Combat">
        <Fallback>
            <Condition ID="IsInCombat"/>
            <Action ID="AbortJob"/>
            <SequenceStar>
                <Action ID="GetTarget"/>
                <Action ID="Move"/>
                <Parallel>
                    <Condition ID="TargetAdjacent"/>
                    <Action ID="AttackTarget"/>

            <Fallback>
                <Action ID="FindFood"/>
                <ForceSuccess>
                    <Action ID="Move"/>
                </ForceSuccess>

                    <Action ID="ReleaseAnimal"/>
                    <Action ID="FinishJob"/>
                </SequenceStar>
                <Action ID="AbortJob"/>
            </Fallback>
        </BB_Precondition>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="JobStandard">
        <SequenceStar>
            <Fallback>

                <Action ID="ClaimItems"/>
                <Action ID="FindTool"/>
                <Action ID="Move"/>
                <Action ID="EquipTool"/>
                <Action ID="GetWorkPosition"/>
                <Action ID="Work"/>
                <Action ID="FinishJob"/>

            <Action ID="AbortJob"/>
        </SequenceStar>

Initially, it sets the first goal, "Goal_a," with coordinates (3.0, 1.5, 0.0, 1.0) and simultaneously executes the "MoveRobot" sub-tree for this goal while taking a snapshot of its status. 
Once this action is completed, it sets a second goal, "Goal_b," with coordinates (-4.0, 2.5, 0.0, 1.0), and again moves the robot towards this new target. 
The tree is structured to repeat this entire sequence once, ensuring the robot can switch between two different navigation targets during its operation.

                        <SubTree ID="MoveRobot" target="Goal_a" />
                        <SnapshotClient />

The behavior tree is designed to manage a robot's navigation in the presence of obstacles by implementing a robust recovery strategy. 
It begins by allowing up to three retries to safely navigate and avoid obstacles. At a rate of one action per second, it recalculates the path to the destination using the Dijkstra algorithm and clears the global costmap to ensure no outdated obstacles interfere with navigation. 
Once a new path is established, the robot follows the adjusted path while also clearing the local costmap. 
Additionally, it has contingency plans activated by updating the goal, which includes essential recovery actions like clearing both local and global costmaps and introducing a short waiting period to facilitate smoother navigation.

  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="3" name="ObstacleRecovery">
      <PipelineSequence name="NavigateAndAvoid">
        <RateController hz="1.0">
          <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="RecalculatePath">
            <ComputePathToPose goal="{destination}" path="{adjusted_path}" planner_id="Dijkstra"/>
            <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalMap-PostObstacle" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
          </RecoveryNode>
        </RateController>
        <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1" name="ProceedAlongPath">

          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalMap-PostObstacle" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
        </RecoveryNode>

        <GoalUpdated/>
        <SequenceStar name="CriticalRecoveryActions">
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearLocalCostmap" service_name="local_costmap/clear_entirely_local_costmap"/>
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="ClearGlobalCostmap" service_name="global_costmap/clear_entirely_global_costmap"/>
          <Wait wait_duration="3"/>
        </SequenceStar>
      </ReactiveFallback>
    </RecoveryNode>

It initiates a recovery process with a maximum of four retries to adjust and navigate along a corrected path based on a given destination. 
First, it reassesses the path by computing a new route using a Breadth-First search and clearing the global costmap to ensure obstacle avoidance. This is executed at a rate of 1.5 Hz. 
After reassessing, if needed, the robot follows the corrected path while also clearing the local costmap. 
In cases where the goal is updated, the system also implements backup recovery actions, which involve clearing both local and global maps and waiting for 1.5 seconds before proceeding. 
These procedures help the robot to adaptively navigate and recover from potential navigation failures.

After finding a new route, the robot attempts to follow it and clears the local costmap for better obstacle avoidance during the journey. If it opts for the second sequence, it moves to Station H after verifying the goal's reachability and continues on its path. It utilizes a fallback strategy to attempt two separate sequences based on the robot's battery level and distance constraints. 
In the first sequence, if the distance from the target1 is at least 2.0 units, the robot computes a path to that target using the Dijkstra algorithm, only proceeding if the battery level is above 30%. 
In the second sequence, if the distance to target2 is at least 1.0 unit, it computes a path to that target using the AStar algorithm, provided the battery level is above 15%. 
After assessing these conditions, the robot follows the computed path to the determined target. 
This behavior allows the robot to adaptively choose a target based on its battery state and distance to ensure efficient operation.

It implements a recovery strategy with up to four retries. The primary function is to continuously update the navigation goal and path while the robot keeps trying to reach its target. 
Using a RateController, the robot computes a new path to the updated goal every 0.6 seconds, pausing briefly between updates. 
If the goal is updated during this process, a fallback mechanism comes into play, which includes clearing the costmap, waiting, and backing up slightly to establish a clearer navigation path. 
This structure allows the robot to adapt dynamically to changes in the environment, aiming to ensure successful navigation even when faced with obstacles.

Actions: [ComputePathToPose (parameters: goal, path, planner_id), Wait (parameters: wait_duration), ClearCostmap (parameters: service_name), BackUp (parameters: backup_dist, backup_speed)]
output:
<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree" BTCPP_format="4">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="4" name="NavigationRecovery">
      <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
        <Sequence>
          <RateController hz="0.75">
            <GoalUpdater input_goal="{goal}" output_goal="{updated_goal}">
              <ComputePathToPose goal="{updated_goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="Greedy"/>
            </GoalUpdater>
            <Wait wait_duration="0.6"/>
          </RateController>
        </Sequence>
      </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
      <ReactiveFallback name="FallbackRecovery">
        <GoalUpdated/>
        <RoundRobin name="FallbackActions">
          <ClearCostmap name="ResetCostmap" service_name="costmap/clear_all_lines"/>
          <Wait wait_duration="0.4"/>
          <BackUp backup_dist="0.3" backup_speed="0.07"/>
        </RoundRobin>
      </ReactiveFallback>
    </RecoveryNode>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The behavior tree defines a robot's navigation recovery logic designed to handle unexpected challenges while navigating. Initially, the robot attempts to update its goal using a planner (Dijkstra) to compute a new path based on the revised goal. It waits for 1.2 seconds before executing the navigation. The robot follows the updated path continuously until it encounters a failure.

If the navigation fails, it triggers fallback mechanisms, which include checking if the goal was updated and executing a series of recovery routines. These routines involve clearing the costmap to reset obstacles, waiting briefly for stabilization, and backing up a short distance (0.15 meters) at a slow speed (0.04 m/s). The design ensures that the robot can adapt its navigation strategy dynamically to maintain progress towards its goal.

Actions: [ComputePathToPose (parameters: goal, path, planner_id), Wait (parameters: wait_duration), FollowPath (parameters: path, controller_id), ClearEntireCostmap (parameters: name, service_name), BackUp (parameters: backup_dist, backup_speed)]
output:
<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree" BTCPP_format="4">
  <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
    <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="6" name="NavigateRecoveryLogic">
      <PipelineSequence name="UpdatedNavigation">
        <RateController hz="0.8">
          <Sequence>
            <GoalUpdater input_goal="{goal}" output_goal="{revised_goal}">
              <ComputePathToPose goal="{revised_goal}" path="{new_path}" planner_id="Dijkstra"/>
            </GoalUpdater>
            <Wait wait_duration="1.2"/>
          </Sequence>
        </RateController>
        <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
          <FollowPath path="{new_path}" controller_id="DynamicPathFollower"/>
        </KeepRunningUntilFailure>
      </PipelineSequence>
      <ReactiveFallback name="FallbackMechanisms">
        <GoalUpdated/>
        <RoundRobin name="RecoveryRoutine">
          <ClearEntireCostmap name="FullCostmapReset" service_name="costmap/clear_all"/>
          <Wait wait_duration="0.5"/>
          <BackUp backup_dist="0.15" backup_speed="0.04"/>
        </RoundRobin>
      </ReactiveFallback>
    </RecoveryNode>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

It begins by configuring the monitoring settings through the "ConfigureMonitoring" subtree, enabling shared access to the blackboard for data storage and updates. 
The main functionality is encapsulated in a fallback structure, where the system continually performs the "Monitoring" action, which logs system status.

The behavior tree is designed to monitor and respond to the charging status of a device or robot. 
It begins by checking the charging status, which determines whether the system is in "Charging" or "Operating" mode. 
If the device is charging and the current parameter set is not already "CHARGING," it reconfigures the monitoring to "CHARGING," announces this state via speech, and changes its facial expression to indicate a "SLEEP" state for 3000 milliseconds. 
Conversely, if the device is operating and the parameter set is not "OPERATING," it switches to "OPERATING," announces that status, and displays a "NEUTRAL" expression. 
This dynamic configuration allows the system to provide appropriate feedback based on its current operational state.

Actions: [ReconfigureMonitoring (parameters: parameter_set, parameter_set_out), Speak (text), FacialExpression (duration, expression)]
output:
<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="MonitoringConfigNew">
        <Sequence>
            <IfThenElse>
                <Condition ID="ChargingStatus"/>
                <Fallback>
                    <BlackboardCheckString return_on_mismatch="FAILURE" value_A="{parameter_set}" value_B="CHARGING">
                        <AlwaysSuccess/>
                    </BlackboardCheckString>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="ReconfigureMonitoring" parameter_set="CHARGING" parameter_set_out="{parameter_set}"/>
                        <Action ID="Speak" text="Charging mode activated"/>
                        <Action ID="FacialExpression" duration="3000" expression="SLEEP"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
                <Fallback>
                    <BlackboardCheckString return_on_mismatch="FAILURE" value_A="{parameter_set}" value_B="OPERATING">
                        <AlwaysSuccess/>
                    </BlackboardCheckString>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Action ID="ReconfigureMonitoring" parameter_set="OPERATING" parameter_set_out="{parameter_set}"/>
                        <Action ID="Speak" text="Operational status"/>
                        <Action ID="FacialExpression" duration="3.0" expression="NEUTRAL"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
            </IfThenElse>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The behavior tree is designed to process and manage the status of a system by evaluating different conditions related to its operational state. 
It begins by checking for an "info" status; if detected, it synchronizes this status with a parameter server, updates the blackboard with the status "INFO," and logs a normal operating message. 
If a warning signal is detected, the tree updates the status to "WARN" in a similar manner. 
Finally, if an error status is detected, it captures the error information and sets the blackboard status to "ERROR." 
This system allows for real-time status monitoring and reporting, ensuring that operational states are clearly defined and communicated.

Actions: [StatusToParamServer (parameters: key, rewrite_stamp), ROSOut (parameters: level, msg, throttle_period)]
output:
<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="StatusProcessingNew">
        <Sequence>
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <Condition ID="StatusInfo" description="Check for info status" error_level="1" key="{key}"/>
                    <Action ID="StatusToParamServer" description="Syncing status" key="{key}" rewrite_stamp="true"/>
                    <SetBlackboard output_key="status" value="INFO"/>
                    <Action ID="ROSOut" level="INFO" msg="System operating normally!" throttle_period="60"/>
                </Sequence>
                <Sequence>
                    <Condition ID="StatusWarn" description="Warning signal detected" error_level="2" key="{key}"/>
                    <Action ID="StatusToParamServer" description="Updating status" key="{key}" rewrite_stamp="true"/>
                    <SetBlackboard output_key="status" value="WARN"/>
                </Sequence>
                <Sequence>
                    <Condition ID="StatusError" description="Error status detected" error_level="3" key="{key}"/>
                    <Action ID="StatusToParamServer" description="Capturing error info" key="{key}" rewrite_stamp="false"/>
                    <SetBlackboard output_key="status" value="ERROR"/>
                </Sequence>
            </Fallback>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

At its core, the system runs a continuous action of "VariantAction" while also utilizing a fallback mechanism to switch between three potential actions based on the value of a variable named `{variant}`. These actions include packing, unloading, and refueling. Each operation is defined in separate sub-trees. For the "Refuel" operation, the robot navigates to a refueling location, checks fuel levels, and executes a path to reach this point. The "Unload" operation similarly involves navigating to a designated unload location and executing an unloading action. Additionally, the "PackUnloadRefuel" combines packing, unloading, and refueling steps sequentially. This behavior tree enables adaptive task handling based on conditions, ensuring efficient robot operation in a dynamic environment.

<root BTCPP_format="4" main_tree_to_execute="MainTree">
    <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
        <Parallel success_threshold="1" failure_threshold="2">
            <Repeat num_cycles="-1">
                <Action ID="VariantAction" value="{variant}"/>
            </Repeat>
            <Fallback>
                <Switch3 case_1="pack" case_2="unload" case_3="refuel" variable="{variant}">
                    <SubTreePlus ID="PackUnloadRefuel"/>
                    <SubTreePlus ID="Unload"/>
                    <SubTreePlus ID="Refuel"/>
                </Switch3>
            </Fallback>
        </Parallel>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="Refuel">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTreePlus ID="GoToRefuel" x_input="0.0" y_input="0.0"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="Unload">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTreePlus ID="GoToUnload" x_input="4.0" y_input="5.0"/>
            <Action ID="objectunload" obj_index="1"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="GoToRefuel">
        <Sequence>
            <Action ID="pathPlanner" number_of_waypoints="{number_of_waypoints_}" waypoints="{waypoints_}" x="{x_input}" y="{y_input}"/>
            <Condition ID="CheckForFuelCondition" value="{fuel_level}"/>
            <Repeat num_cycles="{number_of_waypoints_}">
                <Sequence>
                    <Action ID="ExecutePathAction" w_x="{_w_x}" w_y="{_w_y}" waypoints="{waypoints_}"/>
                    <Action ID="moveRoboterPosition" approachRadius="100" x="{_w_x}" y="{_w_y}"/>
                </Sequence>
            </Repeat>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="GoToUnload">
        <Sequence>
            <Action ID="pathPlanner" number_of_waypoints="{number_of_waypoints_}" waypoints="{waypoints_}" x="{x_input}" y="{y_input}"/>
            <Condition ID="CheckUnloadCondition" value="{number_of_waypoints_}"/>
            <Repeat num_cycles="{number_of_waypoints_}">
                <Sequence>
                    <Action ID="ExecutePathAction" w_x="{_w_x}" w_y="{_w_y}" waypoints="{waypoints_}"/>
                    <Action ID="moveRoboterPosition" approachRadius="100" x="{_w_x}" y="{_w_y}"/>
                </Sequence>
            </Repeat>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="PackUnloadRefuel">
        <Sequence>
            <SubTreePlus ID="packing_subtree"/>
            <SubTreePlus ID="Unload"/>
            <SubTreePlus ID="GoToRefuel" x_input="0.0" y_input="0.0"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="packing_subtree">

                        <Action ID="objectplacement" query="ITEM_0.5_0.3_0.5_0.5"/>

                </ForceSuccess>
            </Repeat>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The behavior tree defines a comprehensive set of tasks performed by an automated agent, covering various job types such as combat, food collection, and animal management. The "CombatSequence" allows the agent to either retreat if a threat is detected or engage in attacking a target if within range. The "UniformManagement" tree manages the agent’s uniform, verifying its condition before either moving or cleaning it before wearing. The "FoodSequence" ensures that the agent can locate and consume food when hungry. The "AnimalJobs" tree outlines a series of actions for capturing animals, determining drop positions, and delivering them. Finally, the "MultipleHaulJob" manages the gathering and transporting of multiple items, including collecting and releasing them appropriately. 

Overall, the behavior tree allows the agent to perform specific tasks efficiently depending on the situation, making it adaptable and versatile.

Actions: 
1. Retreat
2. AcquireTarget
3. Position
4. FireWeapon
5. VerifyUniform
6. Move
7. CleanUniform
8. WearUniform
9. LocateFood
10. CollectFood
11. FindPlaceToEat
12. ConsumeFood
13. PrepareJob
14. WalkToLocation
15. CaptureAnimal
16. DetermineDropPosition
17. DeliverAnimal
18. ProcessAnimal
19. CompleteJob
20. InitializeJob
21. GatherTool
22. UseTool
23. CollectItem
24. ReleaseAllItems
25. FinishJob
26. AbortJob

<root main_tree_to_execute="MainTree" BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="CombatSequence">
        <Fallback>
            <Sequence>
                <Condition ID="ThreatDetected"/>
                <Action ID="Retreat"/>
            </Sequence>
            <Sequence>
                <ForceSuccess>
                    <Action ID="AcquireTarget"/>
                    <Action ID="Position"/>
                    <Sequence>
                        <Condition ID="TargetInRange"/>
                        <Action ID="FireWeapon"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </ForceSuccess>
            </Sequence>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="UniformManagement">
        <Sequence>
            <Action ID="VerifyUniform"/>
            <Fallback>
                <Action ID="Move"/>
                <Action ID="CleanUniform"/>
            </Fallback>
            <Action ID="WearUniform"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="FoodSequence">
        <Sequence>
            <Condition ID="IsHungry"/>
            <Action ID="LocateFood"/>
            <Action ID="Move"/>
            <Action ID="CollectFood"/>
            <ForceSuccess>
                <Sequence>
                    <Action ID="FindPlaceToEat"/>
                    <Action ID="Move"/>
                </Sequence>
            </ForceSuccess>
            <Action ID="ConsumeFood"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="AnimalJobs">
        <BB_Precondition expected="CaptureAnimal" key="JobType">
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <Action ID="PrepareJob"/>
                    <Action ID="WalkToLocation"/>
                    <Action ID="CaptureAnimal"/>
                    <Action ID="DetermineDropPosition"/>
                    <Action ID="Walk"/>
                    <Action ID="DeliverAnimal"/>
                    <Action ID="ProcessAnimal"/>
                    <Action ID="CompleteJob"/>
                </Sequence>
                <Action ID="AbortJob"/>
            </Fallback>
        </BB_Precondition>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="MultipleHaulJob">
        <BB_Precondition expected="HaulSeveralItems" key="JobType">
            <Fallback>
                <Sequence>
                    <Action ID="InitializeJob"/>
                    <Action ID="GatherTool"/>
                    <Action ID="Move"/>
                    <Action ID="UseTool"/>
                    <Inverter>
                        <Sequence>
                            <Inverter>
                                <Condition ID="AllItemsCollected"/>
                            </Inverter>
                            <Sequence>
                                <Action ID="Move"/>
                                <Action ID="CollectItem"/>
                            </Sequence>
                            <Action ID="KeepGoing"/>
                        </Sequence>
                    </Inverter>
                    <Condition ID="AllItemsCollected"/>
                    <Action ID="DetermineDropPosition"/>
                    <Action ID="Move"/>
                    <Action ID="ReleaseAllItems"/>
                    <Action ID="FinishJob"/>
                </Sequence>
                <Action ID="AbortJob"/>
            </Fallback>
        </BB_Precondition>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
        <SubTree ID="Tasks"/>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

It begins by initializing the system and enabling pose detection. 
The robot continuously tracks a person using visual and auditory inputs while monitoring the state of a blackboard variable indicating whether a person is detected. 
If a person is detected, it initiates a series of actions, including confirming the presence of the person, engaging the antenna for communication, greeting the person with a friendly message, and processing spoken inputs. 
If a wake word is detected after 1.5 seconds, it checks for specific requests such as offers for assistance or requests to sing a song, responding appropriately.
This behavior ensures the robot can interact with and assist individuals effectively in various situations.

    <BehaviorTree ID="MainTree">
        <Sequence>
            <SetBlackboard output_key="person_detected" value="0" />
            <PoseDetectionControlAction enable="1" />
            <Fallback>
                <KeepRunningUntilFailure>
                    <Sequence>
                        <TrackAction mode="Track" rate="4" detect_voice="1" turn_base="1" />
                        <AntennaAction rate="0" intensity="10" left_blink_pattern="1" right_blink_pattern="0" />

                                    <SpeechToTextActionClient text="{said}" />

                        </BlackboardCheckInt>

                    <WakeWordDetected since_sec="1.5" />

                        <Sequence>
                            <SpeechToTextActionClient text="{said}" />
                            <TextCompareAction text="{said}" ck_for=".*(how can you help me).*" />
                            <TextToSpeechActionClient msg="I am here to assist you with various tasks!" />

It continuously repeats a fallback mechanism to check the status of sensors, with probabilities determining movement to either "Area C" or "Area D." 
If the sensor check is successful for "Area C" (with an 80% probability), the agent moves there; if not, it checks "Area D" (with a 60% probability) and moves accordingly if that check is successful. 
Once the agent completes its patrol, it moves back to a designated "Base" location. 
This approach ensures the agent can adapt its patrol route based on real-time sensor data, enhancing its operational flexibility.

<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="PatrolTree">
        <Sequence>
            <Repeat>
                <Fallback>
                    <Sequence>
                        <SensorCheck prob="0.8"/>
                        <MoveTo name="patrol_area_C" location="Area C"/>
                    </Sequence>
                    <Sequence>
                        <SensorCheck prob="0.6"/>
                        <MoveTo name="patrol_area_D" location="Area D"/>
                    </Sequence>
                </Fallback>
            </Repeat>
            <MoveTo name="return_to_base" location="Base"/>
        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>
</root>

The behavior tree defines a versatile robotic system capable of performing multiple tasks based on given variants. The system first checks the primary variant; if it matches "pick," "deliver," or "dock," it initiates corresponding actions from the "PickDeliverStart," "Deliver," or "Dock" sub-trees. If the primary variant does not match, it proceeds to an alternative location and utilizes the secondary variant to explore, rest, or return to a starting point. 

The "PickDeliverStart" sub-tree handles the picking and delivering process with the opportunity for default actions if picking requests fail. Each specific task, such as movement to designated areas and executing deliveries, is delineated in separate sub-trees for clarity and reusability.

Actions: 
- VariantAction (parameters: value)
- moveToOtherLocation (parameters: value)
- pickingRequests
- moveToDefaultDeliverArea
- DeliverObject
- moveToDeliverArea
- dock (parameters: angle, x, z)
- moveRoboterPosition
- DetectObject
- approachObject
- validEstimatedPosition
- PatrolArea
- ScanEnvironment
- goToRestArea
- Rest
- navigateHome
- shutDown
output:
<root BTCPP_format="4">
    <BehaviorTree ID="BehaviorTree">
        <Fallback>
            <Sequence>
                <Action ID="VariantAction" value="{variant}"/>
                <Switch3 case_1="pick" case_2="deliver" case_3="dock" variable="{variant}">
                    <SubTree ID="PickDeliverStart"/>
                    <SubTree ID="Deliver"/>
                    <SubTree ID="Dock"/>
                </Switch3>
            </Sequence>
            <Sequence>
                <Action ID="moveToOtherLocation" value="AlternativeLocation"/>
                <Switch3 case_1="explore" case_2="rest" case_3="return" variable="{anotherVariant}">
                    <SubTree ID="Explore"/>
                    <SubTree ID="Rest"/>
                    <SubTree ID="Return"/>
                </Switch3>
            </Sequence>
        </Fallback>
    </BehaviorTree>
    <BehaviorTree ID="PickDeliverStart">
        <Fallback>
            <Sequence>
                <Action ID="pickingRequests"/>
                <SubTree ID="Pick"/>
            </Sequence>

            <Action ID="moveToStart"/>
        </Fallback>

            <Action ID="DeliverObject"/>

    </BehaviorTree>

            <Action ID="DeliverObject"/>

    </BehaviorTree>

        </Sequence>
    </BehaviorTree>

If so, it attempts to determine its global localization, retrying up to three times if necessary. If localization fails, the robot assesses whether it is localized or executes a spin and backup maneuver to reorient itself. 

Next, the behavior tree addresses situations where the robot might be stuck; if it is determined to be stuck, it stops and performs a spin and backup maneuver concurrently. Finally, the robot calculates a path to a specified endpoint and follows that path. This structured sequence of actions ensures the robot can adaptively navigate its environment while handling localization and mobility challenges.

The first parallel section requires the robot to check its patrol route and, if necessary, retry navigating to the next patrol point up to four times in case of failure. If both of these actions succeed, the robot will then transition to a fallback action where it waits for five seconds before marking the patrol as completed by setting a value in the blackboard. This behavior ensures that the robot can handle navigation issues and complete its patrol task reliably while also incorporating a pause to maintain operational efficiency.

  <BehaviorTree ID="PatrolTree">
    <Fallback name="PatrolManagement">
      <Parallel success_count="2" failure_count="2">
        <ReactiveSequence>
          <CheckPatrolRoute route="patrol_path"/>
          <RecoveryNode number_of_retries="4">
            <NavigateToPose goal="next_patrol_point"/>
          </RecoveryNode>
        </ReactiveSequence>
        <Fallback>
          <Wait wait_duration="5"/>
          <SetBlackboard output_key="patrol_completed" value="true"/>
        </Fallback>
      </Parallel>
    </Fallback>
  </BehaviorTree>
</root>

Depending on the values of these coordinates, it instructs one of its arms to move to the face's position using Cartesian control. 

If the conditions for the arm movements are not met, the robot will execute a "LowArms" sub-task to place its arms in a safe position. Additionally, there is a fallback mechanism that activates a speech response if the game state is unknown, where it will announce messages in Spanish.
